assumptions: Synthetic records match observed counts and status/date proportions; this is not a copy of ERPNext business records or a performance test of ERPNext.

Historical child counts use adjacent integer line lengths around the observed mean. Real line-count tails and party/item/warehouse concentration are unknown; 1/5/10/20/50-line classes are separate stress scenarios.
All source Journal Entry categories are balanced manual journal analogues, labeled by category. Payment allocation cannot be inferred from these categories.
Submitted sales have one synthetic full receipt except the observed positive-outstanding count. This reproduces settlement state, not the unknown number or timing of source receipts.

The 14 negative-outstanding source invoices are represented as settled, because the app rejects overpayments. Source returns/manufacturing/subcontracting are not reproduced as equivalent business workflows.
The all-status POS flag proportion is applied independently of document status; it does not establish the submitted-only source POS split.
Stock documents use valid app transfers. Stock openings add one voucher per used warehouse and the configured number of item/warehouse pairs, at 10000 units and rate 9000.
Prices, costs, quantities, tax/discount policy, account use, ownership and user roles are synthetic. Five enabled accounts are admins; normal workload accounts otherwise use Standard ownership rules.
Generated journal, GL and stock-ledger counts follow the application's lifecycle, are compared with source counts and are never padded with unrelated ledger rows.

Historical cancellation reversal dates follow current app behavior. Future source posting dates are excluded. Purchase-order dates use the sales recent/old proportion because their source dates were not profiled.
